title: Council of Europe revives Biden-backed AI rules
dek: Alain Berset has pushed a human-rights focused AI framework that the Biden administration and several European states have already endorsed.
body:
Alain Berset, secretary-general of the Council of Europe, has revived a framework for regulating artificial intelligence that the Biden administration and a number of European countries previously endorsed. The framework is built around protecting human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It was drafted inside the Council of Europe, a small European organization where the measure is better known than it is elsewhere.

## Why it matters

This is a rare instance of the Biden administration aligning publicly with a multilateral text on AI governance rather than a unilateral domestic regulatory push. A framework anchored to human rights, democracy and rule-of-law principles could shape how governments justify limits on particular AI uses, and provides an alternative to approaches that prioritize commercial or national-security objectives. The Council of Europe is not the better-known EU institutions or the OECD; the framework’s origin inside that smaller body helps explain why the text has been relatively unfamiliar outside certain diplomatic circles.

## The details

- Alain Berset is the secretary-general of the Council of Europe and has taken steps to revive this AI regulatory framework.
- The Biden administration has endorsed the framework along with a number of European countries.
- The framework emphasizes respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law as core principles for AI regulation.
- The document was drafted within the Council of Europe, described as a tiny European organization compared with other regional institutions.
- Outside the Council of Europe’s immediate sphere, the framework has remained generally unheard of.

## What to watch

Watch for which governments move from endorsement to concrete policy changes that cite the framework. Also track whether the framework gains visibility in forums dominated by the EU, OECD or G7, where competing AI guidelines already circulate.

Source: [The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/international/6116016-council-europe-ai-framework/)
